subject: Meridian Platform: request for temporary latency tolerance & commercial accommodation
messages:
From: Alex Reynolds <alex@meridian.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2024 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary SLO tolerance + commercial ask

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the integration looks promising. We have an internal go-live window that starts May 6 and a gating item flagged by our platform team: sustained p95 latency needs to be under 200ms for critical routes, otherwise our rollout is delayed. Based on the initial telemetry and our expected burst patterns, we think we will need a short-term operational tolerance while we complete telemetry tuning on our side.

Two asks from Meridian:
- A temporary relaxed latency target (p95 up to 250ms) for the first 12 weeks after go-live, with explicit remediation milestones.
- A commercial accommodation (one-time credit + reduced rate for the first month) to offset ramp risk.

Can Redwood provide these terms, and if so what would the service credit cap and language look like? We can share the integration runbook and projected request profile.

I'll loop in contracts (contracts@meridian.ai) for paperwork. Appreciate quick visibility — our internal release is fixed.

Thanks,
Alex Reynolds
Head of Platform
Meridian Analytics

[attachment: Meridian-SLO-Proposal-v2.pdf]
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex@meridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, contracts@meridian.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2024 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO tolerance + commercial ask

Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask and timeline. Short answer: we can support a temporary latency tolerance with a defined remediation plan, but concessions on SLA/credits and pricing will need Deal Desk + Exec sign-off.

Proposed starter terms (what I'll take to Deal Desk):
- Technical: temporary p95 latency tolerance up to 250ms on three named critical routes for 12 weeks post-go-live. We require a joint runbook, weekly telemetry reviews for first 6 weeks, and a post-mortem at week 12.
- Commercial: one-time onboarding credit (amount TBD) and a 20% discounted usage rate for the first 30 days of production. Service credits for SLA breaches during the tolerance period capped at 5% of monthly invoice (instead of standard 10%).

I attached your SLO proposal and our preliminary cost calc. Ben — can you run numbers and recommend the credit amount and whether the 20%/5% caps are acceptable? Lauren — please flag any legal language that must be added for temporary SLA variance.

I want to be transparent with Meridian: any discount >20% or service credit cap changes beyond the proposed cap will need executive signoff.

Next: Ben will confirm financial impact and I will escalate to Aditya/Marissa for approval if necessary.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Enterprise AE
Redwood Inference

[attachment: Cost-Impact-Calc.xlsx]
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Apr 2024 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Meridian temporary SLO request — recommended commercial approach

Team — forwarding Meridian request. Quick summary and recommendation:

Summary: Meridian requests a 12-week p95 tolerance (250ms) on critical routes and a commercial package: onboarding credit + discounted usage (first 30 days). They asked for the specifics urgently due to a fixed go-live.

Recommended commercial approach:
- Onboarding credit: $45,000 one-time (to offset initial runbook engineering and expected burst cost).
- Usage discount: 25% off list for first 30 days. This is priced to preserve margin while helping them through ramp.
- SLA credits during the tolerance window: capped at 5% of monthly invoice, with requirement for a joint weekly review and a written runbook.
- Additional guardrails: cap the total commercial accommodation (credits + discount) to a not-to-exceed $85,000.

Rationale: 25% discount smooths the number for Meridian and keeps the one-time credit productive. However, because the discount exceeds standard Deal Desk thresholds (20%), this needs approval from Aditya or Marissa. Please approve or provide alternate thresholds.

Attachments: Cost impact calc with scenarios attached.

Ben
Senior Director, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

[attachment: Cost-Impact-Calc.xlsx]
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Apr 2024 14:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Meridian temporary SLO request — recommended commercial approach

Ben — thanks for the breakdown. I support the proposed technical guardrails and the requirement for a joint runbook + weekly telemetry reviews. Commercially I am comfortable with the onboarding credit and a discount in that band provided we hard-cap total accommodation. Please adopt the following conditions if approved:

1) Discount capped at 25% and limited strictly to the first 30 days; no extensions without exec re-approval.
2) Total not-to-exceed accommodation cap of $85,000 as proposed.
3) Service credit cap stands at 5% of monthly invoice during the tolerance window and reverts to our standard terms after 12 weeks.
4) Add a clause for immediate escalation to Redwood SRE and Meridian if p95 exceeds 350ms for more than 3 consecutive hours — temporary mitigation includes prioritized pairing and burst capacity at Meridian's expense.

Lauren — please draft the amendment language for the temporary SLO variance and the accommodation cap. If the final numbers adhere to these constraints, I will sign off. If the discount exceeds 25% or the accommodation cap is raised, I will need Marissa's explicit approval.

Aditya
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2024 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: APPROVED: Meridian temporary SLO variance + commercial accommodation (conditional)

All —

I reviewed the proposal and approve the temporary SLO variance and commercial accommodation subject to the conditions Aditya outlined. Key points I expect to be enforced before final sign:
- Written runbook accepted by both parties and a kickoff call scheduled within 48 hours of contract amendment execution.
- Accommodation not-to-exceed $85,000; discount capped at 25% for first 30 days only.
- Weekly telemetry review invites synced to both teams for the first 6 weeks.
- Legal to include an explicit clause that the temporary variance auto-terminates at week 12 unless both parties agree in writing to extend.

Tessa — you have authority to communicate these approved terms back to Meridian and instruct Legal to prepare the amendment (cc: Lauren). Keep me in the loop on final SOW execution.

Marissa Cole
Chief Revenue Officer
Redwood Inference
